title: The Japanese Rule To Lose Visceral Fat in 3 Weeks
summary: Doctor Mike Diamonds (a former medical doctor turned fitness coach) films in Japan and presents three Japanese cultural habits he frames as a way to lose visceral fat in three weeks. The three 'rules' are: (1) Hara Hachi Bu — eating to 80% fullness, supported by tactics like drinking green tea/matcha/sparkling water 20 minutes before meals, chewing 20-30 times, using chopsticks, and the PFC eating order (protein first, fiber second, carbs last); (2) Interval Walking Training — alternating 3 minutes fast and 3 minutes slow walking for 30 minutes; and (3) the Metabo Law — Japan's government-mandated waist-size measurement plus mandatory school nutrition education. The throughline is creating a 'natural Ozempic effect' by slowing eating and digestion so the brain registers fullness (which he says takes ~20 minutes). It is a health/lifestyle persuasion video citing some studies, not a rigorous scientific review, and it doubles as a funnel to his coaching program.

title: RT by @bcherny: This is a super exciting release - Claude Fable 5 is the same underlying model as Mythos but with added safeguards. The benc
summary:
RT by @bcherny: This is a super exciting release - Claude Fable 5 is the same underlying model as Mythos but with added safeguards. The benchmarks are great and it's SOTA on everything by a margin but I'll add that *qualitatively* also, this is a major-version-bump-deserving step change forward (imo of the same order as Claude 4.5 was in November), peaking especially for long problem-solving sessions on very difficult problems. You can give it a lot more ambitious tasks than what you're used to, the model "gets it" and it will just go, and it's never felt this tempting to stop looking at the code at all (but don't do this in prod!). The model still has quirks that people will run into and the safeguards are configured to be a little too trigger happy for launch, which can hopefully be tuned over time.

I feel a lot of things changing as working software increasingly comes out on a tap. The Jevon's paradox kicks in and I feel my own demand for software growing substantially. You can ask for anything - explainers, visualizers, dashboards, bespoke single-use apps (e.g. a full wandb that is hyper-specific just for your project), you can 10X your test suite, auto-optimize code, run giant research projects with custom HTML for the results, anything! "Free your mind" (Matrix ref). Really looking forward to all the things people build!
